searchText: > I changed my graffiti, so I don't show up there... I'll check my logs in the morning. Late here now. I know that Afri's Teku validators have been down for a week now. <@!573787335796326400> nooo... I restarted them last week. They must have crashed again. Sorry was out for the weekend. Let me check the logs. Indeed ... ``` 05:23:30.113 FATAL - PLEASE FIX OR REPORT | Unexpected exception thrown for nioEventLoopGroup-3-12 io.netty.channel.ExtendedClosedChannelException (See log file for full stack trace) ``` That one isn’t actually fatal (log level reduced and I’m hunting it down to get rid of it). There was a period of ninfinalisation over the weekend though so I suspect you’ll find an out of memory error in there which really was fatal. <@557201004060213248> - is 357 one of yours? Apparently it hasn't made any attestations since 30 May. The whole block 312 - 439 is the same. yes, those are all mine. I restarted them on June 1st but apparently they were still not fixed I'm just about to pull latest master and try again wow my validator has 208 peers on witti Witti is having small problems. It looks like there is no split, but the latency is high, and there are many small forks and reorgs On the left: state table (incl skip slots) see how block-root stays the same sometimes (= skip slot) and even reverts back to an older one a few times (= parallel fork) I've been indexing the Witti chain for analysis/charts, will share those later this week. our prysm witti node went out of sync: ``` prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 11:58:00" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 11:58:15" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 11:58:30" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 11:58:45" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 11:59:00" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 11:59:15" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 11:59:30" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain ``` also after restarting it is unable to find any peers The eth1 client warning is because Goerli had some issues. Not sure why that would make prysm stop syncing eth2 though looks like the prysm goerli node is out of sync or the goerli issues do affect the eth2 chain those are our last log messages when the node went out of sync: ``` prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:28:12" level=info msg="Finished applying state transition" attestations=6 attesterSlashings=0 deposits=0 prefix=blockchain proposerSlashings=0 voluntaryExits=0 prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:28:16" level=info msg="Peer disconnected" active=0 peer=16Uiu2HAkxVKcqXfKLjSccKrxzrhgiRYLDq5FwtHUgF42gFtZ6U98 prefix=p2p prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:28:16" level=info msg="Verified and saved pending attestations to pool" blockRoot=28bc55ad6713 pendingAttsCount=8 prefix=sync prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:50:30" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:50:45" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:51:00" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:51:15" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:51:30" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:51:45" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:52:00" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-08 09:52:15" level=warning msg="eth1 client is not syncing" prefix=powchain ``` <@!203220829473996800> witti should be working again 😄 is anyone scraping witti peers btw and compiling page with their ENR records btw? also, how's everyone dealing with `noise` vs `secio`? both or just one? <@!604062686623432740> is doing scraping And for noise vs secio you should ask in the <#646778960830660623> channel, I'm not 100% sure about latest client approaches there > is anyone scraping witti peers btw and compiling page with their ENR records btw? <@449019668296892420> Do u need a list of enrs? I'm a bit interested in a live list of peers on the network, what versions they're on etc - if I have a list I can filter peers I'd like to test connecting to, more easily For a quick look, the lighthouse API has a neat peerstore dump API endpoint I'll get you a list, should cover most of witti, but not all, unlike scraping <@!449019668296892420> https://gist.github.com/protolambda/ebdd737ad491e3ff43c374f4795126cb > I'm a bit interested in a live list of peers on the network, what versions they're on etc - if I have a list I can filter peers I'd like to test connecting to, more easily <@449019668296892420> I'll DM u a list from the last crawl I did > wow my validator has 208 peers on witti <@!557201004060213248> do u mind sharing the peerstore for this? i'm curious if they are all witti nodes <@203220829473996800> i thought the client implementation (prysm,teku..) are not public? the libp2p identify protocol is active currently, I think we should disable it for privacy though > <@!449019668296892420> https://gist.github.com/protolambda/ebdd737ad491e3ff43c374f4795126cb <@!203220829473996800> i'm seeing peers with a head slot in the 60,000 range. They don't have the "Sync_Status":"Behind" or "Synced" property...instead it is "Advanced". Does this mean they have a different fork-digest? You need to ask <@!498009160982724610> about the exact meaning of those peerstore fields It's probably just older sync info that stuck around after a sync, while the node moved on > It's probably just older sync info that stuck around after a sync, while the node moved on <@!203220829473996800> im too dumb to understand those words However in the lh code i see this: ``` /// The peer has greater knowledge about the canonical chain than we do. Advanced { info: SyncInfo }, ``` > It's probably just older sync info that stuck around after a sync, while the node moved on <@!203220829473996800> so if what u are saying is true, then these peer counts could be inflated by nodes that are no longer online and only lazily removed No what I'm saying is that at some point the peer may have synced from my lighthouse node, or my node synced from them, and it never removed that knowledge from the peerstore after the sync. Best guess though, I'm not familiar with this peerstore approach of Age
